# Fixed response stream served by the OpenConfig fake gNMI agent
# (github.com/openconfig/gnmi/testing/fake/gnmi/cmd/fake_server).
#
# This is a text-proto encoding of the fake.Config message. The "fixed"
# generator streams these gnmi.SubscribeResponse messages verbatim, which is
# why it is used here: every field the receiver has to interpret is pinned by
# this file rather than synthesised by a random generator.
#
# A fresh response queue is created per Subscribe RPC, so a reconnect replays
# the whole stream instead of yielding an empty one.
#
# The notifications below deliberately carry a non-empty `prefix`. A gNMI
# target is free to split a path between the notification prefix and the
# update path, and the receiver must rejoin them; keeping the split here is
# what makes that assertion meaningful.

target: "fakedut"
client_type: GRPC_GNMI

# Hold the stream open once the queue drains, instead of closing it. Without
# this the receiver would see the session end and redial in a loop.
disable_eof: true

fixed: {
  # Integer counters under a keyed list element. Exercises: prefix/path
  # rejoining, uint64 -> int datapoint (no float rounding), and list keys
  # surfacing as datapoint attributes rather than as part of the metric name.
  responses: {
    update: {
      timestamp: 1700000000000000000
      prefix: {
        origin: "openconfig"
        elem: { name: "interfaces" }
        elem: { name: "interface" key: { key: "name" value: "eth0" } }
        elem: { name: "state" }
        elem: { name: "counters" }
      }
      update: {
        path: { elem: { name: "in-octets" } }
        # Larger than 2^53, so a value routed through a float64 would lose
        # precision. This is what pins counter64 handling.
        val: { uint_val: 9007199254740993 }
      }
      update: {
        path: { elem: { name: "out-octets" } }
        val: { uint_val: 54321 }
      }
      update: {
        path: { elem: { name: "in-errors" } }
        val: { uint_val: 7 }
      }
    }
  }

  # A second interface, to prove the key attribute actually varies per
  # datapoint rather than being hardcoded.
  responses: {
    update: {
      timestamp: 1700000000000000000
      prefix: {
        origin: "openconfig"
        elem: { name: "interfaces" }
        elem: { name: "interface" key: { key: "name" value: "eth1" } }
        elem: { name: "state" }
        elem: { name: "counters" }
      }
      update: {
        path: { elem: { name: "in-octets" } }
        val: { uint_val: 111 }
      }
    }
  }

  # A string leaf, which has no numeric representation and is emitted as an
  # *_info metric carrying the value as an attribute.
  responses: {
    update: {
      timestamp: 1700000000000000000
      prefix: {
        origin: "openconfig"
        elem: { name: "interfaces" }
        elem: { name: "interface" key: { key: "name" value: "eth0" } }
        elem: { name: "state" }
      }
      update: {
        path: { elem: { name: "oper-status" } }
        val: { string_val: "UP" }
      }
    }
  }

  responses: { sync_response: true }
}
